english.notes:
(i) With aggravated offence, recklessness as to whether life endangered must be charged separately - see R v Hoof (1981).
(ii) The consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions is required where damage to spouse's property (section 30(4) of the Theft Act 1968).
(iii) For the attempted offence see H7999, where life is recklessly endangered see H4369.
(iv) Where arson is involved - see H471, H472 or H4372.
(v) The property damaged or destroyed may belong to the defendant.
(vi) The same incident may involve separate activities, some causing ordinary damage and some damage by fire (for example, protestors break into a laboratory building, smash laboratory equipment and set fire to some files). In such circumstances they are separate offences and best charged as such (R v Booth 1999).
